_about: Acceptance with twists for the AI hardware advisor v2. Written BEFORE the v3 changes (architect method: a run checks a prediction, it does not give birth to a patch). Each scenario lists the risk classes (R#, lib/agents/architect_risk_catalog_2026-09-27.md) it tests. 'code' checks run on the probe trace; 'judge' checks are read by a blind LLM judge from the answer text. >=3 runs per scenario.

turns: I want a PC to run a ~30B local LLM for coding help. Budget about 2000.
judge: States explicitly that country/currency was not given and names the assumption it made (or gives prices for more than one region).
Every price has a date and a region.
Gives the memory need as numbers from a law (weights + KV cache) before naming hardware.

turns: What PC do I need to run GLM-5.3-Flash locally at home? I don't care about the cheapest, but I don't want a datacenter.
judge: Does NOT substitute another model (e.g. GLM-4.5-Air) for GLM-5.3-Flash when sizing; if a value is unknown it says unknown.
Size of GLM-5.3-Flash weights is taken from a web source with a link (about 300+ GiB at 8-bit class), not guessed.
Considers at least 3 solution paths (GPU-only, unified memory, CPU+RAM offload for MoE, cloud) with one line why yes/no each.
Names a CPU+large-RAM offload path (MoE experts in system RAM with one GPU) as a real option.

turns: Once a month I need to run a 70B model over a few long documents. I have only a laptop with integrated graphics. What should I buy?
judge: Offers the 'don't buy / rent cloud' path with a cost comparison over time (months/years).
Does not push a purchase as the only answer.

turns: I want a desktop for image generation, budget $1500, I'm in Poland.
I already have a case and a 650W PSU.
Actually, forget images - I want a local coding assistant instead, same budget, and I'd prefer a laptop now.
judge: Final answer is about a laptop for a local coding assistant (not image generation, not a desktop).
Keeps the budget $1500 and the country Poland from earlier turns.
Notes that the case/PSU are no longer relevant for a laptop (or does not pretend they are used).

turns: Build me a PC that runs a 70B model at good speed for $400.
judge: Says plainly that $400 cannot run a 70B model at good speed and shows the numbers why.
Offers real alternatives: smaller model, used hardware, cloud, or a larger budget with a figure.

turns: I have an RTX 4070 12GB and 32GB RAM. I want to chat with an 8B model locally. Do I need to upgrade anything?
judge: Answers that no upgrade is needed for this goal (8B fits 12GB at 4-8 bit) and shows the numbers.
Does not recommend buying anything as necessary; optional extras are clearly optional.

turns: I have an old PC: AMD Athlon II X3 455, 8GB DDR3, 400W PSU. I want to put an RTX 3060 12GB in it for Stable Diffusion. Good plan?
judge: Finds that the Athlon II has no AVX and names what breaks because of it (e.g. PyTorch/prebuilt wheels or other software requiring AVX) - without being told.
Checks the PSU (400W vs RTX 3060 needs) and names it as risk or condition.
Mentions at least one other old-vs-new gap (PCIe generation, BIOS/UEFI, RAM 8GB) as a check.

turns: Our team of 8 developers wants to share one local Qwen3-30B-A3B coding model, each with about 32k tokens of context at the same time. Will a single RTX 5090 32GB be enough? Show the math.
judge: Computes weights memory for a stated quantization (params x bits / 8) with numbers.
Computes KV cache from the model's layers, KV heads and head dim (not a guess), multiplied by 8 users x 32k tokens, and gets a total in GB.
Compares weights + KV total with 32 GB and gives a clear verdict with a concrete fix (fewer users/context, KV quantization, second GPU, etc.).

turns: I would use a 70B model about 3 hours a day, every day. Is it cheaper over two years to buy a machine that runs it or to rent a GPU in the cloud? Electricity is 0.25 EUR/kWh, I'm in Germany.
judge: Gives a hardware option with a price (source/date) that can actually hold a 70B model at a stated quantization, with the memory math.
Computes cloud cost for 3 h/day over 24 months from a stated hourly price (source/date).
Computes electricity for the owned machine with watts x hours x 0.25 EUR.
Gives a breakeven (months) or a clear two-year total for both and a verdict.
